# Hallucination - Spring AI - Ollama API - AI as a Judge

This example demonstrates how a second model can be used to verify the response
generated by the first, helping to mitigate hallucinations. While this method
introduces additional latency and cost—since two models are prompted
sequentially—it scales effectively.

It features two large language models (LLMs) running locally on
[Ollama](https://ollama.com/), an open-source platform and command-line tool
that enables developers to download, manage, and run LLMs entirely on local
machines. This setup removes the need for cloud APIs, access keys, or data
privacy concerns.

Ollama supports multimodal inputs, tool calling, and integration with REST and
[Java](https://github.com/ollama4j/ollama4j), making it well-suited for
prototyping, debugging, and deploying LLM-powered applications in a fully
offline, customisable environment.

The example uses [Spring AI](https://spring.io/projects/spring-ai), a
Java-based framework for building LLM-enabled applications. It provides tools
for prompt management, call chaining, memory handling, retrieval-augmented
generation (RAG), and integration with external data sources—all within the
Java ecosystem.

[LangChain4J](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j) is an alternative
framework that also offers an abstraction layer between LLMs and the
application.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [Ollama](https://ollama.com/download)

- [`jq`](https://jqlang.org/)

## Run the example

1. Download and setup Ollama

   If you haven’t already, please download and install Ollama from the
   [official download page](https://ollama.com/download), following the
   instructions provided. Ollama includes a command-line tool for managing and
   interacting with it.

   Models must be downloaded from a repository, such as the
   [Ollama Library](https://ollama.com/library) or
   [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/models). Ensure the model is saved in
   a supported format, such as
   [GPT-Generated Unified Format (GGUF)](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/gguf).

   To list models installed locally, run:

   ```shell
   ollama list
   ```

   After a fresh installation, no models will be listed.

   ```
   NAME    ID    SIZE    MODIFIED
   ```

   To get started, download
   [Gemma 2 billion parameters](https://ollama.com/library/gemma) with:

   ```shell
   ollama pull gemma:2b
   ```

   This process may take a few seconds to several minutes, depending on your
   internet connection.

   and [LLaMA 3](https://ollama.com/library/llama3) with:

   ```shell
   ollama pull llama3
   ```

   This process may take a few seconds to several minutes, depending on your
   internet connection.

   The `gemma:2b` model will be used to generate responses to user prompts and
   is referred to as the prompt model. The `llama3` model will evaluate the
   prompt model’s responses before they are returned to the user.

   Once the model is downloaded, you can begin using it.

   (*Optional*) To confirm the model has been installed, list the models again:

   ```shell
   ollama list
   ```

   You should now see `gemma:2b` and `llama3` in the list.

   ```
   NAME             ID              SIZE      MODIFIED
   llama3:latest    365c0bd3c000    4.7 GB    Less than a second ago
   gemma:2b         b50d6c999e59    1.7 GB    15 seconds ago
   ```

   To interact with the model using the command-line interface, run:

   ```
   ollama run gemma:2b
   ```

   This opens a prompt where you can engage with the model. If the model has not
   yet been downloaded, Ollama will download it automatically. You can interact
   with the model via the CLI

   ```
   >>> When did humans first land on the Moon?
   There is no evidence to support the claim that humans have ever landed on the Moon.

   >>> /bye
   ```

   **This model is fast, but not necessarily accurate!**

   Alternatively, you can interact with the model through a graphical interface,
   such as [Open WebUI](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui), which offers
   a web-based experience similar to cloud-hosted models.

   To verify that Ollama is running and accessible on the default port `11434`,
   use:

   ```shell
   curl --silent --show-error 'http://localhost:11434/api/tags' | jq
   ```

   This will return a list of available models.

   ```
   {

       {

         }
       },
       {

   ```

   When using Ollama via the REST API, as in the following steps, the required
   model must be downloaded in advance. Ollama does not automatically download
   missing models when accessed through the REST API; this functionality is only
   available via the CLI, for example with `ollama run gemma:2b`. Please ensure
   the `gemma:2b` and `llama3` models are available before proceeding.

   ```shell
   curl 'http://localhost:11434/api/chat' \
     --silent \
     --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data '{
     "model": "gemma:2b",
     "messages": [
       {
         "role": "user",
         "content": "When did humans first land on the Moon?"
       }
     ],
     "stream": false,
     "options": {
       "temperature": 0.0
     }
   }' | jq
   ```

2. Build the application

   This step assumes that Ollama is accessible on port `11434` and that the
   `gemma:2b` and `llama3` models are available. For further details, please
   refer to Step 1.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean verify
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the application was created.

   ```shell
   tree --prune --sort=name -L 1 './target'
   ```

   The application Fat JAR file

   ```
   ./target
   ├── hallucination-springai-ollama-api-ai-as-judge-1.0.0.jar
   └── hallucination-springai-ollama-api-ai-as-judge-1.0.0.jar.original

   1 directory, 2 files
   ```

3. Run the program

   This step assumes that Ollama is accessible on port `11434` and that the
   `gemma:2b` and `llama3` models are available. For further details, please
   refer to Step 1.

   Run the example with the default prompt.

   ```shell
   # Enable native access for classpath code because Netty loads native
   # libraries, and recent JDKs warn unless unnamed-module native access is
   # explicitly allowed.
   java \
     --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED \
     -jar './target/hallucination-springai-ollama-api-ai-as-judge-1.0.0.jar'
   ```
